newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power steady in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power steady in quiet trading.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. held steady Monday versus Friday's levels in quiet trading, market sources said.
"It's a quiet, quiet day," said a Midwest-based marketer.
The biggest player in Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC), Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) was closed today in observance of the U.S. Columbus Day holiday.

Modest electricity demand combined with return of Georgia Power Co's 1,162 MW Vogtle nuclear power unit 2 from scheduled refueling kept spot SERC prices approximately in Friday's ranges, market sources said.
Vogtle 2's resumption to service eased the recent transmission constraints at the TVA and Southern Co transfer point, and allowed more spot supply into the Florida pennisula, traders said.
"It's slightly better, schedulings are not cut as early," one SERC industry source said.

Amid to thin activity, next-day electricity for firm, peak delivery into the northern region of TVA was notationally assessed at $14.00-$15.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), flat from Friday's quote for Monday.
Friday, TVA was heard offering next-day peak power for Tuesday in $19.00-$19.50 range.
Down at the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Tuesday was valued at $22.50-$23.50, up from a range of $22.25-$22.50 on Friday for Monday delivery.

"It's very flat in terms of generation," said a SERC trader, referring to tight production capability in Florida due to the ongoing shutdown of the 825 megawatt (MW) Crystal River 3 nuclear station in Florida.
The Red Level, Fla., power unit, operated by Florida Power Corp was shut Sept 2 to replace a leaky section of a line that feeds lubrication oil to its turbine shaft.
But restart of the plant remains unknown until NRC completes safety review of a recent modification to one of the reactor's emergency diesel generator.
